clue.text: Cook a rib in a new way — with skate wings

indicators.note: doing something in a new way means rearranging, so these letters are shuffled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its two outer letters, one at each side

explanation.surface: A chef tries a fresh recipe combining ribs with the fins of a skate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a new way' rearranges A RIB into BRAI; the wings of skate are S and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Braising is a cooking method: slow simmering in a little liquid in a covered pot.

clue.text: One might feel exposed in this dawn light west of rocky Uist

definitions.text: One might feel exposed in this

indicators.note: in a down answer, west of is read as placed before the next piece

parts.note: the dawn of something is its birth or beginning
daylight, so light can mean day

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady, so the letters of the island name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Early sunshine lights up the Hebridean island of Uist, with rugged scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: Uist is an island in Scotland's Outer Hebrides; 'rocky' rearranges its letters into SUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorous idiom for nakedness: the skin one was born in, in which anyone would feel exposed.

clue.text: Certain muscles seen on duck that gets plucked

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, the figure O
a lute is a stringed instrument played by plucking

explanation.surface: Bodybuilding talk about strong muscles beside a duck being plucked for the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen on' just joins the pieces. 'That gets plucked' looks like the duck being prepared, but it is a separate piece: the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute certainty is complete sureness, so absolute here is a synonym for certain.

clue.text: See 1
Uncovering dodgy jewellery

parts.note: rum in British slang means odd or suspicious
bling is flashy showy jewellery

explanation.surface: Police exposing a ring dealing in suspect jewels.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbling someone in British slang means finding them out, so it is a synonym for uncovering.

clue.text: Nasty piece of work that calls for beautician?

definitions.meaning: read whimsically as a plain-looking client who visits the beauty parlour

explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for a menacing person; also literally an unattractive client of a beauty salon.

clue.text: Launch attack on party

definitions.meaning: to hit or criticise someone hard
an informal word for a lively social gathering

explanation.definitionFit: Bash means both to strike or lambast, and colloquially a big festive get-together.

clue.text: Hit peak with this cool guitar?

parts.note: ice is something cool or cold
axe is musicians' slang for a guitar

explanation.surface: A rock star hits the top of the charts with a cool-looking guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit peak' suggests chart success, but it means striking a mountain summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer's tool for cutting steps and gripping, used to strike icy summits.

clue.text: Pull over half-sister and threaten to go out

indicators.note: over in a down clue asks for the word to be flipped round

parts.note: a tug is a sharp pull

indicators.note: half of the word sister is taken, here its second three letters

explanation.surface: A girl tugs at her half-sister and threatens to leave the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TUG into GUT; the second half of sister is TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A candle flame gutters when it flickers and seems about to die, a verb of near extinction.

clue.text: Rough game's uncontrolled movement

parts.note: RU is rugby union, the game, with the S of the possessive
a tic is an involuntary twitch

explanation.surface: A sports report blaming a messy match on erratic play.
explanation.walkthrough: RU (rugby union) plus the 's gives RUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Rustic means simple and rough-hewn, as in country furniture, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: It's used for canvassing — and for canvassing

definitions.meaning: a leaflet handed out when canvassing voters
a canvas cover pitched over a tent, 'and' leading in the second sense

explanation.definitionFit: A fly-sheet is both a printed handbill and the outer waterproof cover of a tent.

clue.text: 'Sad Club' with name like that's dead

parts.note: a disco is a night club
so means in that way, like that
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: A gloomy nightclub called 'Sad Club' is as lifeless as its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Disconsolate means downcast and unable to be comforted, a close synonym for unhappy.

clue.text: Beatles song sampled backwards in Purple Haze

indicators.note: backwards says the hidden letters are read backwards
sampled says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Beatles track is sampled in reverse on Jimi Hendrix's Purple Haze.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1965 Beatles single and film title, so the definition names it as one of their songs.

clue.text: Problem thumb

definitions.meaning: to thumb a lift, to hitchhike

explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag; to hitch is to thumb a ride from passing drivers.

clue.text: Shaft or source of light in fire

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: to axe someone is to fire them from a job

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A beam or ray of light seen in the flames.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fire' looks like flames, but means dismiss, giving AXE.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or shaft on which a wheel turns.

clue.text: Yes, marm, ignore the old creep

indicators.note: ignore means leave out, so letters are dropped from the words

parts.note: ye is the old form of the, as in Ye Olde Tea Shoppe

explanation.surface: A servant bows and says 'Yes, marm', ignoring the old toady.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop YE from YESMARM to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To smarm is to behave in an oily, ingratiating way, the verb sense of creep.

clue.text: Tabloid boss blew his top

parts.note: a rag is a low-grade newspaper
ED is the editor, boss of a paper

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor flies into a rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Raged is past tense of rage, flying into fury, matching the idiom for losing one's temper.

clue.text: Chair cover mascara stain made a mess of

indicators.note: making a mess of something jumbles it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A make-up smudge has ruined the cloth on an armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a mess of' rearranges MASCARA STAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth laid over a chair back to protect upholstery from hair oil.

clue.text: Conclude bug is risk

parts.note: to end is to conclude
to bug someone is to annoy or anger them

explanation.surface: Someone decides an insect is a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger something is to put it at risk, the verb sense of risk.

clue.text: Weapon spoiling inconclusive armistice

indicators.note: spoiling means ruining, so these letters are scrambled
inconclusive means without its end, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A sword threatens to wreck a fragile ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inconclusive' drops the final E of armistice; 'spoiling' rearranges ARMISTIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved oriental sword, a kind of bladed arm.

clue.text: Canine co-star bombed over the water

indicators.note: a film that bombed was a flop; here it means the letters are wrecked and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A film starring a dog flopped badly overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Transoceanic means across or beyond the ocean, so crossing over the sea.

clue.text: Drink may turn cold, served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: can and may both express permission
a go is a turn
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A drink may go cold if it is left after being served.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a spirit one would drink.

clue.text: Sweet girl taking political leader round

indicators.note: taking means holding inside

parts.note: a cutie is an attractive girl

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An attractive girl escorts a politician around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' looks like the containment signal, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cup-tie is a knockout match in one stage of a cup competition, as in a fourth-round game.

clue.text: Work dries up — or some of it in recession

indicators.note: in recession says the hidden letters are read backwards
some of it says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Employment vanishes when the economy goes into recession.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is a creative composition, a musical or literary piece.

clue.text: One over on course for instance stopping lout coming back

indicators.note: coming back asks for everything to be read in reverse
stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: yob is British slang for a lout
eg stands for exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A golfer goes one over par because a hooligan keeps getting in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over' is golf's language, not cricket's. YOB is British slang for a hooligan; 'stopping' then 'coming back' make YEGOB, read in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a bogey is a score one stroke over par on a hole.

clue.text: Wrong actor tackling Romeo

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so one wraps round the other

parts.note: a ham is an overacting player
R is Romeo in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An actor makes a mess of playing Romeo.
explanation.definitionFit: Harm and wrong are synonyms as nouns for injury or damage done to someone.

clue.text: Magic cocktail lacking vermouth

indicators.note: lacking means without, so letters are removed

parts.note: a mojito is a rum cocktail with mint and lime
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It

explanation.surface: A cocktail that has lost its magic without the vermouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Mojo is a charm or magical power, now often meaning personal magnetism.

clue.text: Order a kir — it's an aniseed drink

indicators.note: order as a verb suggests arranging, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: fodder for the anagram; that the letters also run forwards across 'Order a kir' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A bar customer asks for a kir, a blackcurrant aperitif, which turns out anise-flavoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' rearranges A KIR; 'it's an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Raki is a Turkish and Balkan spirit flavoured with anise.

clue.text: Fanciful and unthinkable assuming one's a Liberal

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: not on means unacceptable, out of the question
one is I as the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone thinks an idea fanciful and out of the question, supposing they are a liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' is British idiom for unacceptable; 'assuming' lodges the Roman one inside, and 'Liberal' is the old UK party, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Notional means imaginary or existing only in theory, close to fanciful.

clue.text: Mother took round good grub

parts.note: ma is mother

indicators.note: round as in going round something means surrounding it, so one piece is wrapped about the other

parts.note: got is past tense of get, took

explanation.surface: Mum brought tasty food round.
explanation.definitionFit: A maggot is a fly larva, the insect sense of grub.

clue.text: Old American Conservative hero's not entirely eager

parts.note: the word given; the possessive adds no letters

indicators.note: not entirely says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: A politician of the past was a heroic, if half-hearted, figure.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEN without its last letter gives KEE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cherokee are a Native American people, here referred to as indigenous Americans of old.

clue.text: Daily Echo

definitions.meaning: a daily newspaper, here the British tabloid
to echo is to copy or reflect

explanation.definitionFit: The Mirror is a British daily paper, and to mirror is to reflect or imitate.
